original_question: Let G be a finitely presented group, and let H be a finitely generated subgroup of G whose membership problem in G is solvable, meaning there is an algorithm deciding whether a given word in G represents an element of H. Must the word problem in G itself then be solvable, that is, must there be an algorithm deciding whether a given word represents the identity element of G?
target_in_paper: No direct match to the draft exists in arXiv:1902.10093; the closest official paper-faithful statement is Conjecture 2 (Introduction; developed in §4): "Classical de Sitter solutions with intersecting sources are unstable."
correct_elements: The draft is at least phrased as a yes/no implication-style research question asking whether one condition forces another. Beyond that structural feature, it does not match the paper’s subject, objects, hypotheses, or terminology.
missing_details: The paper is not about finitely presented groups, subgroup membership, or algorithmic decidability; it is about classical de Sitter solutions in 10d type II supergravity with Op/Dp sources.

The paper restricts the problem to a standard ansatz: smeared solutions on a 6-dimensional compact group manifold with fluxes whose coefficients are constant in a flat basis; this restriction is essential because it makes the conjectures mathematically well-defined.
The sources are Op/Dp of a single fixed size p >= 3, preserving 4d Lorentz invariance.
The relevant distinction is between parallel and intersecting sources, where intersecting means N > 1 sets of parallel sources wrapping different internal directions rather than the same ones.

The ambient equations and constraints must be part of the setup: the 10d Einstein equation, dilaton equation of motion, flux equations of motion, flux Bianchi identities, and orientifold projection constraints.

The paper’s notion of instability must be stated: it is a classical perturbative instability, not merely a flat direction; in 4d language it means at least one tachyonic scalar, equivalently a negative eigenvalue of the Hessian of the scalar potential and thus eta_V < 0.
The 4d consistent-truncation/gauged-supergravity viewpoint is part of the nearby context used to formulate and test the conjecture.
The draft omits the group-manifold, smearing, constant-flux, and source-intersection assumptions that are central to the paper’s actual question.
refined_question: Within the standard ansatz studied in arXiv:1902.10093—namely smeared classical de Sitter solutions of 10-dimensional type II supergravity with Op/Dp sources of a single fixed size p >= 3, on a 6-dimensional compact group manifold, with fluxes having constant coefficients in a flat basis—must every solution with intersecting sources (that is, with N > 1 sets of parallel Op/Dp sources wrapping different internal directions) be classically perturbatively unstable?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, in the associated 4-dimensional consistent truncation, must every such de Sitter critical point have at least one tachyonic scalar, so that the Hessian of the scalar potential has a negative eigenvalue and eta_V < 0?
justification: The draft does not match the subject of arXiv:1902.10093 at all. Since no statement in the paper concerns groups or decision problems, the closest official statement by logical form is Conjecture 2, introduced in the Introduction, made precise using the paper’s standard ansatz in §§2.1-2.2, and translated into a precise 4d instability criterion in §2.3. Section 4 is then devoted specifically to attempting to prove this conjecture.
